MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ADJOURNED MEETING
  AUGUST 16, 2021

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates
  was called to order at 6:00 p.m. in Linden H. Chandler Preserve, 95 Buckskin Rd., Rolling Hills
  Estates, California by CHAIR POPE.

  2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  CHAIR POPE led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, Pope, Retz, Romanelli

  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  Persichina

  STAFF PRESENT:  Alexa Davis, Assistant City Manager
  Michael Goldsmith, Maintenance Superintendent
  Daniel A-Haja, Community Services Coordinator

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF
  JULY 19, 2021

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted that the disruption that ended the Commission
  meeting in July was not included in the minutes and wondered if they should be. Assistant
  City Manager (ACM) Davis responded that staff will discuss with the City Attorney on how
  to proceed.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI moved, seconded by CHAIR POPE TO APPROVE AS
  FOLLOWS:

  TABLE THE PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF JULY 19,
  2021 UNTIL THE NEXT MEETING.

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  None

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE AGREEMENT

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
AUGUST 16, 2021
   ACM Davis presented a brief overview of the staff report. She noted an update will be
  added to the cancellation policy to include a credit towards the following year should the
  County or State prohibit large outdoor events as a result of a public health concern, but
  was awaiting the final Agreement from Pageantry Parades.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked about the fourth wave of COVID and what information is
  available in regards to the event as more locations are doing vaccine checks and requiring
  masks. ACM Davis responded the County is tracking numbers but to date there is no
  indication that events will be closed down or have a required vaccine check-in, however
  masks may be required or recommended. She reported that the subcommittee will meet
  and discuss a possible route change as the mall is not opened for events yet and can
  additionally discuss alternative options to consider the public health precautions. Staff
  recommends coming back to the Commission in September with an update.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ stated he would prefer holding off until September to analyze the
  cancellation policy and include a provision that the firm provide advanced notice before
  incurring any costs.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK suggested postponing approval of the contract to
  September stating that much of the public health concern might not change within that
  time.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if there could be anything the City could do to modify social
  distancing for the event. CHAIR POPE noted the empty sections on the route that could
  be used to spread people around and use markings on the ground such as snowflakes.
  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith noted the increase of cost in lighting if the route
  were to spread out more. ACM Davis suggested convening the subcommittee for further
  guidance and alternatives.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked what the deadline was for the agreement. ACM
  Davis stated that September would be the latest preferred.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if schools bands were still practicing. ACM Davis
  responded that they are still practicing.

  CHAIR POPE stated the Commission will postpone a decision until September.

  Item 6 E Taken out of order:
  E.  PVPLC GEORGE F CANYON ANNUAL REPORT (VERBAL REPORT)

  Chris Sarabian from the Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy present the annual
  report and noted the impact COVID had on the previous year. He explained that
  transitioning staff to online classes was difficult but digital field trips and Family Nature
  Club were great successes. The virtual experiences allowed for greater access to a wider
  range of schools due to videos being accessible on YouTube. The Nature Center has
  been open to the public in-person for limited hours since May 8. Masks are recommended
  when children are present outdoors, and all indoors, and County protocols are being
  followed. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith noted working on cutting back the
  invasive poison oak along the George F Canyon trail.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
AUGUST 16, 2021
   CHAIR POPE asked how future school field trips will be planned to the Nature Center.
  Mr. Sarabian responded that a hybrid online/in-person field trip is being proposed but not
  yet finalized.

  ACM Davis added that the status of the Nature Center remodeling project is moving
  forward. City Council has approved the architect firm agreement in July and an
  Environmental Impact Initial Study consultant agreement is approved which will
  incorporate neighborhood concerns that have been heard such as parking and noise
  issues. Future use considerations will return to the Commission for continued discussion
  at the October meeting. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI suggested the public be made
  aware of the discussion when it is scheduled.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted the use of a scavenger hunt at the Nature Center
  for kids. Mr. Sarabian responded that the Nature Center does have something similar
  available as an app-based hunt and gives out patches for completion.

  Item 10 A was taken out of Order
  10.  PARK TOURS

  A.  CHANDLER PRESERVE (VERBAL REPORT)

  The Commission proceeded with the Park Tour guided by Mr. Sarabian of the Palos
  Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy. Mr. Sarabian discussed the PV Butterfly and the
  important of the Preserve habitat. He detailed the various vegetation grown to support the
  habitat and the support received by local university students and studies.

  Meeting resumed order with 6B:

  B.  CONCERTS IN THE PARK

  ACM Davis presented a brief overview of the staff report. COMMISSIONER RETZ
  suggested connecting with a local band as well as Remember the Music Festival contacts.
  Discussion ensued about the two options presented between the Palos Verdes Peninsula
  Symphonic Band or hiring a production company with a band.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked who the concert should be attracting. CHAIR POPE stated
  that it should be a small community event that could be open to a variety of ages. ACM
  Davis responded that the event could follow the movie night template the City already
  holds.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK stated concern that the symphonic band may not attract
  families with children, however it was suggested that they could possibly play genre that
  would be attractive such as show tunes or Disney music. It was further recommended
  that there could be a singalong style with the symphonic band.

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER RETZ TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
AUGUST 16, 2021
   RECOMMEND THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE A CONCERT AT ERNIE
  HOWLETT PARK WITH THE PV SYMPHONIC BAND ON OCTOBER 23, 2021 IN
  THE AFTERNOON AT A COST OF $2,500.

  AYES:  Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, Pope, Retz, Romanelli
  ABSENT:  Persichina

  C.  HILLS ARE ALIVE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Coordinator A-Haja provided a brief overview of the August 2021
  event. Race participants dropped to 131 this year with sponsorship funds remaining about
  the same. Revenue is projected to be on par with previous years as this is the second
  year without a race director. Some notable suggestions for the race this year are to
  improve access to water station #3 for HAM Radio access and chip timing for runners.

  He reported subcommittee debrief meeting will be held soon to provide input for next
  year’s planning.

  D.  TRACY AUSTIN DOUBLES TOURNAMENT (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Coordinator A-Haja reported that Ms. Austin is available three Fall
  weekends: October 2 & 3, November 6 & 7 or November 13 & 14 and that the
  subcommittee will meet soon to start planning this event.

  F.  TABER GROVE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  ACM Davis reported the Taber Grove development is completed. She shared that
  Maintenance Superintendent and his crew did a great job of clearing and preparing the
  site for the work done by the contractor. She stated that in coordination with the Taber
  Family and Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy a park dedication will be planned,
  originally thought September 2 but possibly August 31 and an invitation will go out once a
  final date is selected.

  7.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith reported that Highridge fencing will soon be
  replaced by vinyl instead of the originally planned wood. He explained that in further
  research, he believes vinyl to be a worthwhile and long-lasting replacement option and will
  provide a cut out so people can walk through.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  ACM Davis asked the Commission if staff should return with a proposal for summer
  concerts in the park in January along with movie night suggestions. The Commission
  concurred.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
AUGUST 16, 2021
   8.  STAFF ITEMS

  None

  9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF JULY 27, 2021

  Received and filed.

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF AUGUST 10, 2021

  Received and filed.

  11.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  HIGHRIDGE ART MURAL

  Staff will return with an updated based on Commission feedback at the next meeting in
  September.

  B.  ROCKBLUFF PLAYGROUND STRUCTURE

  Staff expects to bring a proposal to the Commission in September.

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  COMMISSIONER RETZ moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK to:

  ADJOURN THE MEETING AT 7:33 PM TO THE NEXT ADJOURNED PARK AND
  ACTIVITIES MEETING ON SEPTEMBER 20, 2021 AT 7:00 P.M., WHICH WILL
  MEET AT CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT 4045 PALOS VERDES DRIVE
  NORTH.

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  _____________________________
  Daniel A-Haja  Lisa Pope
  Community Services Coordinator  Park & Activities Commission Chair

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
AUGUST 16, 2021
